THE CHANGE: (3) BEST-FIRST -- the order INSPECTS up to 3 town containers (no clicks) and ranks every usable copy: never spent (<= 10 uses), then tier (netherite > diamond > iron > stone > golden > wooden), then uses left; it revisits the winner, revalidates the exact copy (slot, name, wear) and takes it; a copy proven gone re-ranks, an unreachable one STOPS the order (never a worse copy instead); a copy not strictly better than the held tier is never taken; with a full bag and a full chest the bag's worse pickaxe itself is traded (mode-2, by identity, revalidated at the click). An upgrade order also fires for a bot whose best usable pickaxe is below iron (30-min cooldown), suppressed only when BOTH branches are ruled out by complete negative evidence (_pick_best <= held in every town container; ingots ruled out). (1) IRON UPGRADE -- with no copy of iron or better: a complete plan of <= 2 take visits from what the inspection saw (3 ingots + 2 sticks, or wood for them; a table within the craft's 32-block search or planks for one), room for every take made at the first visit within that chest's live capacity, >= 60 s of clock, and a per-bot 30-min cooldown (+ 0-5 min name stagger) charged before the first mutation; prerequisites first, ingots LAST after a re-plan against the live bag; exactly the deficit; then the existing craft skill (craftsync); success only with verification=server AND the order's own recount showing iron_pickaxe +1. A failed craft leaves the ingots in the bag and deposit keeps up to 3 (bankable iron_upgrade_reserve) while the best usable pickaxe is below iron; no retry within 30 min. Ingot evidence per container with QUANTITY (_ingot_seen), from this visit's contents. Every row carries a structured LEDGER in args (held, took_tier, took_uses, best_seen, best_valid, gone, craft, produced, srv = cumulative server change, plan, transform = recipe-chain names consumed, complete). licence.note: withdraw-01 is on the whole fleet (c902d6f), so _withdraw_pick rows exist on the control too; the withdraw2 build is told apart by the structured ledger in the row's args (complete=true). The read's ARMS line (control_rows_with_ledger) must stay 0.

require.name: bots crafting or wanting a pickaxe (craft rows naming _pickaxe)

draw_exposure.note: The target population is bots at town whose best usable pickaxe is below iron (most of the fleet: 31/80 held an iron pickaxe over 72 h) -- any pool qualifies; the require line only rejects a dead pool.

exposure.note: Ready = >= 5 canary withdraw_pick orders AND >= 1 control bot at town with a usable pickaxe below iron.

own_lines.note: G1: a canary row whose cumulative server change (args srv) shows a fall of a name not in plan nor transform (the craft chain's own names: iron_ingot, stick, planks, log). A death within 60 s is excused and reported. Rows without a complete ledger are UNKNOWN (ledger_unknown_g1), never a pass.
G2: a pickaxe taken with <= 10 uses left (args took_uses, or detail uses=).
G5: a pickaxe taken whose tier is below best_valid (the best copy observed this order and not proven gone).
G6: outcome=crafted_iron without craft=server AND srv iron_pickaxe >= +1 on a complete ledger. Incomplete = UNKNOWN (ledger_unknown_g6).
Arms: the withdraw2 ledger on a control row means the pools are mixed. BLOCKS KEEP.
Every canary order row (except aborted/error) carries the ledger; a row without it means the canary runs another build or the gates are blind. BLOCKS KEEP.
POSITIVE CONTROL: control bots at town with a usable pickaxe below iron exist and this query sees them. BLOCKS KEEP.

primary.note: REPORTED, NOT GATED: confirmed iron_pickaxe crafts per bot-hour (_craft_sync item=iron_pickaxe confirmed=yes), DiD; share of withdrawn pickaxes that are iron or better, DiD (iron_share_did); bots holding iron or better, DiD (iron_holders_did); withdrawn pickaxes by tier per arm and period; crafted_iron rows. No null scale exists for these metrics yet: a single read is not a result; INCONCLUSIVE is a legitimate close. POWER: confirmed iron_pickaxe crafts are ~1 per fleet-hour (68 in 72 h, positive control 10-06), so a 5-bot canary expects ~0.2 in 3 h on the control rate: the craft rate and holders DiD will usually be INCONCLUSIVE at +180/+360; the tier share of withdrawn pickaxes moves first (control 1 of 13 iron in the dry run).

harm.note: Unchanged: the two-death floor (OWNER 2026-09-11) and gather_ratio < 0.43 of control, from immobiledid. A held cursor freezes the bot (admission refuses every skill): watch intervention_bots and _reflex_stuck.

teardown.note: THREE STEPS: drop-ins, clear canary_pool, restart the pool's bots 12 s apart; then confirm the live versions. A restart DROPS any stack a held cursor carries (sandbox: disconnect drops the cursor whatever the room) -- check intervention rows before the restart and name any held bot.
